question: Which statement best describes The route.ts file?
options: A Route Handler lives in a `route.ts` (or `route.js`) inside the `app/` directory; its folder path becomes the URL. `app/api/users/route.ts` serves `/api/users`. A segment can have a `page.tsx` OR a `route.ts`, not both, because both own the same path.

Handlers use the standard Web Platform `Request` and `Response` (and `NextRequest`/`NextResponse` extensions). You read from the `Request` and return a `Response` — the same primitives as Fetch and edge runtimes, so the knowledge is portable.

Get JSON with `await request.json()` (or `.formData()`/`.text()`), query params via `new URL(request.url).searchParams` or `request.nextUrl.searchParams`, and dynamic route segments from the second argument's `params` (e.g. `app/api/users/[id]/route.ts`).

You implement an endpoint by exporting async functions named for the HTTP verbs you support: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`. A request to an unimplemented method returns 405 automatically. Each function runs on the server only.
